clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within the following year: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to your mother's every evening; your father took night shifts and distanced from your mother; your uncle Anton drank at lunch with a warning at work; his wife Celeste left him in August; your mother lay awake over them; and your brother Callum had ear infections all winter. Your grandmother's functioning came back in May 1979 when she took a job at the library, and these shifts settle there.

clusters.name: Odette's bed rest, 1984
clusters.reason: Around your mother's bed rest in March 1984: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep the house, argued with your father over how she kept it, your brother Callum stammered again after a year free of it, and you could not sleep unless your father sat by your bed. Your mother gave birth in September, and the shifts settle with that arrival and after.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's diagnosis of Parkinson's disease in September 1986, within the following decade: your grandfather Ambrose took over her cooking and appointments; your father phoned his father every night for news; Hazel had a bad fall in 1988, steadied briefly on new medicine in 1988, then declined again in 1991 when she could no longer dress herself. Your father and your uncle Lyle argued over who should help in 1989. Your grandfather gave up his workshop in 1996 and hardly left her side. Your father drank most evenings from 1993, and your aunt Pearl had panic spells at the wheel from 1993. Your mother took Hazel to the clinic twice a week from 1992 and your aunt Mavis came to stay one week in four to nurse her sister. Hazel moved to the Fairlie nursing home in June 1997, and the family settled there.

clusters.name: Callum leaving home, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum leaving for a job up north in May 1999: your father and Callum argued most nights over his plans; your mother could not settle at the thought of him so far away; your father missed days at work and sat up late in the garage; your sister Ines skipped school most of that autumn; your mother took Ines with her everywhere. Your sister's functioning came back by August 2000 when she was back at school full days and passed her exams, and the shifts settle there.

clusters.name: Hazel's death, 2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's death in January 2003: you could not sleep more than a few hours a night, stopped going to the bookshop and were let go in May, and dreaded buses and crowded shops, going out only after dark. You took a job at the garden centre in November and were sleeping through the night again. These are your own shifts, and no one else's shows in these months.
